title: Computer-Aided Inspection Planning Software — Overview and definition
t: Computer-Aided Inspection Planning Software — Overview and definition
description: Plans CMM and scanner measurement strategies from CAD with GD&T.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Plans CMM and scanner measurement strategies from CAD with GD&T. Computer-aided inspection planning reads CAD with PMI, selects probes and styli, plans touch points and scan paths, and simulates the inspection for collisions. Real implementations include PC-DMIS, Calypso, PolyWorks Inspector, and GOM Inspect. It optimizes the point budget for the tightest tolerances and outputs DMIS programs.
capabilities: PMI import and automatic feature recognition
Probe/stylus selection and qualification planning
Touch-point and scanning-path generation per GD&T callout
Collision simulation of probe, part, and fixture
DMIS and native CMM program output

body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Teaching ladder for Computer-Aided Inspection Planning Software, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (PMI import and automatic feature recognition). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: PMI import and automatic feature recognition and Probe/stylus selection and qualification planning. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Coordinate measuring machine (CMM) programming software) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
